eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast models from Environment Canada and NOAA indicate Toronto’s daily maximum temperature on August 16 will likely peak in the mid-20s Celsius, with consensus favoring 26–27 °C under partly cloudy skies and moderate southwesterly flow. Lake Ontario’s moderating influence and potential afternoon lake-breeze development introduce uncertainty in the precise peak, as localized cooling or delayed heating can shift the observed high by 1 °C. Historical August baselines average near 25 °C, while current humidity and weak upper-level support limit stronger warming. Traders assign nearly equal weight to 26 °C and 27 °C outcomes because final readings depend on the exact timing of any showers or clearing, with Environment Canada updates expected throughout the afternoon to refine the official daily maximum.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecasts from the China Meteorological Administration and regional models indicate a coastal high near 32–33°C for Qingdao on August 17, driving the tight market split between those outcomes. Persistent subtropical high pressure supports subsidence warming, yet marine air advection and potential afternoon sea-breeze development along the Yellow Sea coast introduce downward pressure on peak readings. Model spread remains modest but centers on whether boundary-layer mixing and any late-day convection will cap or allow the extra degree. Updated CMA guidance and afternoon observational trends ahead of market resolution will clarify the final maximum.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Incheon Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 18 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Incheon Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/kr/incheon/RKSI.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from the Korea Meteorological Administration and supporting models position 30°C as the leading outcome for Seoul-Incheon's August 18 maximum, reflecting a post-heatwave moderation with increased cloud cover, scattered showers, and lighter winds limiting daytime heating compared to early-August peaks near 38–39°C. Recent shifts toward more stable but humid summer conditions, including 20–60% precipitation probabilities and typical late-August climatology of 30–32°C highs, underpin the market's tight clustering around 29–31°C (over 86% combined implied probability). Model consensus remains the key near-term driver, though any rapid clearing or delayed rainfall could nudge readings higher before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: The active southwest monsoon (habagat) driving persistent cloud cover, scattered showers, and thunderstorms over Metro Manila is the dominant factor capping daytime maxima. PAGASA guidance through August 19 indicates partly to mostly cloudy conditions with 50-60% rain probability, reducing solar insolation and keeping peaks near or below the 28-29°C range that holds roughly 73% implied probability. This aligns with climatological suppression during peak monsoon periods, when seasonal averages of 30-31°C are frequently moderated by 2-4°C. Recent model consensus and ongoing moisture flux reinforce trader positioning around these thresholds, though any temporary monsoon break could briefly allow readings near 30°C before resolution on August 18.
